items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: an old friend of mine came by -- Davey Tough, Davie Duff, a drummer

ctx.x: finally got myself out of debt, and my wife said, 'Well, we have all the bills paid up, so when you get paid today, you can go down to F&F -- that was where all the musicians used to go to get their suits made. In New York. So she said to go down to F&F and have you a couple of suits made.

So I said okay. So, I go to the theatre, and we played the first show. Well, just before I went onstage, an old friend of mine came by -- Davey Tough, Davie Duff, a drummer -- he came by, and I sent the valet out to get a bottle for us, and while he went to get this bottle, they called 'all on', so I had to go onstage.

We got paid right after that show. I couldn't wait; I was the first one, because every theatre we played, we had a room set up where we all would go in this room and either shoot crap or play blackjack. So I ran down to this room and grabbed the cards, and said, 'My bank was $175' -- that is what I was making at that time. So there was Lucky, Taft Smith, Deak Deke Watson and Bill Kinney -- these were the four guys I had to deal to.
